items.text:
1. Lighthouses help vessels identify coastlines and hazards.
2. Many lighthouses stand near rocky shores.
3. A lighthouse’s light can be visible for miles in clear weather.
4. Lighthouse keepers once maintained lamps by hand.
5. Fresnel lenses concentrate light into powerful beams.
6. Some lighthouses use flashing patterns to identify their locations.
7. Lighthouse lights are called beacons.
8. Fog signals can warn ships when visibility is poor.
9. Some lighthouses are built on offshore rocks.
10. Lighthouse towers are often painted in contrasting colors.
11. Stripes can make a lighthouse easier to spot by day.
12. A lighthouse’s height affects how far its light can be seen.
13. Islands often have lighthouses to guide approaching vessels.
14. Modern lighthouses may operate automatically.
15. Solar panels can power some remote lighthouse equipment.
16. Lighthouses can mark the entrances to harbors.
17. Some lighthouse buildings include living quarters.
18. Lighthouse designs vary by region and era.
19. Stone is a common material in historic lighthouse construction.
20. Cast-iron towers were used for some lighthouses.
21. Lighthouses have helped reduce shipwrecks.
22. Mariners use nautical charts to learn lighthouse locations and signals.
23. Each lighthouse’s light pattern can serve as a distinguishing characteristic.
24. Some lighthouses have rotating lights.
25. Lighthouse lenses may contain many glass prisms.
26. The Statue of Liberty served as a lighthouse for a time.
27. Some decommissioned lighthouses are open to visitors.
28. Coastal erosion can threaten lighthouse foundations.
29. Lighthouses appear in art and literature as symbols of guidance.
30. Lighthouse museums preserve stories about maritime navigation.
